subject: Dedicated capacity queue priority and SLA safeguards for SolarFlare AI
messages:
From: Anika Bose <anika@solarflare.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask: dedicated queue priority & fallback behavior

Hi Markus / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — SolarFlare's evaluation team is pushing hard to a decision and we have a few specific asks on the Dedicated SKU behavior before committing. Attaching our draft SLA request and a short CSV with April traffic samples (queueing-metrics-apr.csv).

High level: we need deterministic tail latency under production load for inference (P99 latency target) and a clear fallback for bursty nightly batches. Some concrete items we'd like Redwood to confirm or propose:
- Throughput guarantee: sustained concurrent inference capacity (we can commit to N GPUs but need an upper bound on concurrent requests / tokens/sec).
- Queueing behavior: how preemption and eviction work when nightly batch windows run; whether we can get a soft-priority lane or inflight headroom.
- Failure credits & remediation: what crediting or mitigation you can offer if P99 targets are missed more than X times / month.

Can you loop in ops/serving engineering to validate what guarantees are feasible? We plan to finalize procurement the week of 4/18, so a short technical note + contract language would be ideal.

Proposed next step: 30-min tech sync (Markus + David) to review queue semantics and an outline of measurable SLOs.

Attachments: SolarFlare_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf, queueing-metrics-apr.csv

Thanks —
Anika Bose
Head of ML Infrastructure
SolarFlare AI

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Anika Bose <anika@solarflare.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: dedicated queue priority & fallback behavior

Folks, quick technical read based on the CSV and our runtime behavior. High-level conclusions and recommended guardrails: 

1) What Dedicated gives you:
- A reserved GPU pool means predictable aggregate throughput but not strict per-request deterministic latency unless we reserve inflight slots.
- Our runtime supports a priority queue and a configurable "burst buffer" (KV/prefix cache retention + reserved concurrency slots).

2) Recommended SLOs we can realistically commit to (assuming you reserve at least 8 GPUs):
- P99 tail latency for standard generation requests (<=512 tokens): <= 350 ms under steady-state traffic up to 60 concurrent generation sessions per reserved GPU (rough heuristic; exact mapping depends on model and quantization).
- Throughput floor: sustained token throughput equivalent to X tokens/sec per GPU (we use calibrated benchmarks; propose we embed numbers in the SOW once we pick model variant).

3) Queueing / preemption behavior options (trade-offs):
- Soft-priority lane (recommended): allocate 10-15% of inflight concurrency as reserved for priority inference. Nightly batch jobs are throttled to background lane and cannot evict priority slots. This preserves tail latency but reduces batch throughput during windows.
- Hard eviction (not recommended): allow preemption of active sessions — reduces tail guarantees and risks partial outputs.

4) Burst & headroom: we can provision a short-lived burst buffer (15% of pool) to absorb brief spikes; this requires a small capacity reservation uplift (billable).

5) Observability & breach detection: we'll export token-level latencies and queue backlog metrics to your SIEM and Redwood Console; breaches are defined by rolling-window P99 violations (e.g., >3 windows in 24 hours triggers remediation).

Next steps I can do: a short appendix with calibrated numbers for your model(s) and a suggested prioritization config snippet (example below). I can deliver that by EOD 4/12 if you want it in time for contract drafting.

Example prioritization config (informal):
- reserved_concurrency_ratio: 0.12
- burst_buffer_percent: 0.15
- nightly_batch_schedule: 02:00-04:00 UTC -> throttled_to_background
- breach_policy: rolling 1h windows, if P99 >350ms for 3 windows -> trigger mitigation + alert

Happy to jump on the 30-min sync and walk through.

— David
David Kim
SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Anika Bose <anika@solarflare.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: dedicated queue priority & fallback behavior

Anika / Markus — thanks, David's recommendations are exactly the level of detail procurement needs. A few commercial points from our side: 

- Pricing impact: reserving a 15% burst buffer and a 10-15% reserved_concurrency uplift will increase committed spend by ~8-12% depending on SKU. I can run a tailored model once you confirm target GPU count and model.
- Remediation: standard approach is tiered credits. Proposal: if agreed P99 target is missed for >=3 distinct 1h windows in a month, we apply a 5% invoice credit for that month; if >=6 windows, 12% credit, capped at 25%. We can include a service credit matrix in the SOW addendum.
- Contract mechanics: we'll draft an SLA addendum and include the prioritization config as an appendix. SolarFlare will need to confirm the exact model variant and committed GPUs to finalize numbers.

Action items for procurement:
1) SolarFlare confirms committed GPU count and preferred model variant (e.g., rdx-16q or rdx-32f) — affects throughput calibration.
2) We (Redwood) deliver an SLO appendix with calibrated tokens/sec and latency numbers (David by EOD 4/12).
3) Redwood legal to produce SOW addendum + DocuSign packet (Lauren).

I will prepare a draft addendum and send via DocuSign link for review. Markus — can you coordinate the exec signature timeline?

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Anika Bose <anika@solarflare.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: dedicated queue priority & fallback behavior — recap & next steps

All — quick recap and agreed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks: 

Agreed technical approach (tentative):
- Soft-priority lane with reserved_concurrency_ratio: 12% and burst_buffer_percent: 15% (billing uplift ~10% as Lauren noted).
- P99 target: <=350 ms for <=512-token generation under committed load (final numbers in SLO appendix).
- Nightly batch policy: scheduled 02:00-04:00 UTC will be throttled to background lane (no eviction of priority).

Commercial / contract items:
- Lauren to draft SOW addendum with remediation credit matrix and send DocuSign link (ETA: 4/14).
- David to provide calibrated SLO appendix with tokens/sec mapping for SolarFlare's chosen model (ETA: EOD 4/12 — please confirm model variant if possible).
- Anika to confirm committed GPU count by 4/15 so we can finalize pricing.

I'll set a 30-min wrap-up call on 4/13 at 10:00am PT to sign off on the tech appendix if needed.

Thanks everyone — Marking this as high priority.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
